[32601 Advanced Project Management | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject is focused on the so-called “soft” aspects of Project management. In this subject, you'll grasp the intricacies of project management within a global business context, focusing on human and organisational dynamics, project governance, and the evolving role of project managers. You'll develop critical skills in teamwork, analysis, and research, enabling you to tackle complex business solutions effectively. Learning is interactive and collaborative, featuring in-class flipped learning sessions, discussions, and group projects that encourage critical thinking. You'll also undertake individual research, formulating and defending your own perspectives on relevant issues.

[32601 Advanced Project Management | Learning and teaching activities]
This subject is taught through a one hour lecture and two hour tutorial each week on the City campus. The lectures and tutorials are structured to reflect how projects operate in the real world—blending theory, discussion, and scenario testing into one continuous and interactive learning session. 

Each week, you’ll explore key concepts in advanced project management, including leadership, ethics, stakeholder engagement, governance, and delivery frameworks. These ideas won’t just be discussed in theory—they’ll be applied immediately through realistic project scenarios, ethical dilemmas, or stakeholder challenges. You'll be encouraged to test your assumptions, make decisions, and reflect on the outcomes in real time. 

Workshops are highly collaborative and designed to simulate the workplace. You’ll work in project teams across the semester to respond to briefs, engage with case studies, and co-develop a group tender submission. These teams are expected to manage their own work through tools such as Kanban boards, team roles, and meeting notes—just as you would in industry. 

You’ll also complete individual reflections where you critically evaluate your leadership style, emotional intelligence, and decision-making. It is critical for assessment purposes these reflections are grounded in evidence from your team experience and supported by theory introduced in class. 

This subject integrates thinking and doing throughout. Participation, initiative, and reflection are essential—for both learning current practice, and for enhancing the skills expected of a professional advanced project manager.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32601 Advanced Project Management | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Analyse ethical responsibilities, social impact, and cultural inclusivity in the planning and delivery of complex projects. (B.1)
SLO2: Evaluate complex projects and propose evidence-based solutions for continuous improvement in advanced project delivery and professional contexts. (D.1)
SLO3: Evaluate personal leadership, decision-making, and ethical challenges in complex project environments, using critical self-reflection and feedback to improve professional practice and support ongoing personal development. (F.1)

[32601 Advanced Project Management | Requisites]

[32601 Advanced Project Management | Additional subject details]
Professional standards
Students enrolled in the Master of Professional Engineering should note that this subject contributes to the development of the following Engineers Australia Stage 1 competencies: 

- 1.4 Discernment of knowledge development and research directions within the engineering discipline. 

- 2.4 Application of systematic approaches to the conduct and management of engineering projects.

- 3.1 Ethical conduct and professional accountability.

- 3.4 Professional use and management of information

- 3.5 Orderly management of self and professional conduct.

Recommended studies
It is recommended that students enrolled in this subject have knowledge have prior knowledge of project management principles and some level of relevant practical experience
